message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference list of the **federal statutory holidays that create a “long weekend”** (i.e., a holiday that falls on a Friday or a Monday, giving you a three‑day weekend) in Canada for the calendar year 2023.  
(If you’re looking at a specific province, keep in mind that many provinces have their own holidays—see the “Provincial notes” section below.)

| Date | Day of Week | Holiday | Notes |
|------|-------------|---------|-------|
| **Jan 2** | Monday | *Observed* New Year’s Day | New Year’s Day fell on Sunday Jan 1, so the holiday was observed on Monday Jan 2. |
| **Apr 7** | Friday | Good Friday | A federal holiday that always falls on the Friday before Easter Sunday. |
| **May 22** | Monday | Victoria Day | Celebrated on the Monday preceding May 25 (Victoria Day). |
| **Jul 3** | Monday | *Observed* Canada Day | Canada Day fell on Saturday Jul 1, so the holiday was observed on Monday Jul 3. |
| **Sep 4** | Monday | Labour Day | Celebrated on the first Monday in September. |
| **Oct 9** | Monday | Thanksgiving | Celebrated on the second Monday in October. |
| **Nov 11** | Monday | Remembrance Day | Celebrated on the Tuesday after Thanksgiving, but it is a statutory holiday in most provinces. |
| **Dec 25** | Monday | Christmas Day | Celebrated on the first Monday in December. |

> **Boxing Day (Dec 26)** falls on a Tuesday in 2023, so it does not automatically create a long weekend unless you take an extra day off.

---

### Provincial / Territorial Notes

| Province/Territory | Additional Long‑Weekend Holiday(s) in 2023 |
|--------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| **Ontario** | Family Day – Feb 20 (Monday) |
| **British Columbia** | Family Day – Feb 20 (Monday) |
| **Alberta** | Family Day – Feb 20 (Monday) |
| **Manitoba** | Family Day – Feb 20 (Monday) |
| **Saskatchewan** | Family Day – Feb 20 (Monday) |
| **New Brunswick** | Family Day – Feb 20 (Monday) |
| **Nova Scotia** | Family Day – Feb 20 (Monday) |
| **Prince Edward Island** | Family Day – Feb 20 (Monday) |
| **Quebec** | St. Jean‑Baptiste Day – Jun 24 (Wednesday) *(not a long weekend)* |
| **Newfoundland & Labrador** | St. John’s Day – Jun 24 (Wednesday) *(not a long weekend)* |
| **Northwest Territories** | N/A |
| **Yukon** | N/A |
| **Nunavut** | N/A |

> *Family Day* (the first Monday in February) is celebrated in most provinces except Quebec, Newfoundland & Labrador, Northwest Territories, Yukon, and Nunavut. It creates a long weekend in those provinces.

---

#### Quick Takeaway

In 2023, the federal holidays that give you a natural three‑day weekend in Canada are:

1. **Jan 2** (Observed New Year’s Day)  
2. **Apr 7** (Good Friday)  
3. **May 22** (Victoria Day)  
4. **Jul 3** (Observed Canada Day)  
5. **Sep 4** (Labour Day)  
6. **Oct 9** (Thanksgiving)  
7. **Nov 11** (Remembrance Day)  
8. **Dec 25** (Christmas Day)

Add the provincial Family Day (Feb 20) if you’re in one of the provinces that observe it, and you’ll have a total of nine long weekends for the year.  

Feel free to plug this list into your holiday‑planning app!
